key_insight: TaxoMIL turns whole-slide diagnosis into hierarchy-aware text generation, using taxonomy constraints to keep predictions aligned with clinical coarse-to-fine reasoning.
clinical_relevance: It may improve pathology decision support by reducing label violations and making slide-level outputs more semantically consistent with real diagnostic taxonomies.
method: Dual-head Transformer decoder generates both coarse-level and fine-level diagnostic text.
Taxonomy-guided objectives shape the label embedding space and constrain predictions to the clinical hierarchy.
Built for multiple instance learning on whole-slide images to support slide-level diagnosis.
evidence_signal: The paper reports experiments on three diverse WSI datasets, where TaxoMIL outperformed state-of-the-art MIL classifiers and VLM-based generative methods.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on a well-defined taxonomy and careful constraint design; results may be less robust if the clinical label hierarchy is incomplete or noisy.
paper_title: TaxoMIL: Taxonomy-Constrained Learning for Hierarchical Whole Slide Image Analysis
